definitions.explanation: A shop where one gets a haircut, especially a traditional barbershop catering mainly to men. Can also refer to the barber who works there. A casual, everyday word.

examples.japanese: {散髪屋|さんぱつや}に{行|い}く。
{駅前|えきまえ}の{散髪屋|さんぱつや}で{髪|かみ}を{切|き}った。
examples.english: I got my hair cut at the barbershop in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}は、{父|ちち}に{連|つ}れられて{近所|きんじょ}の{散髪屋|さんぱつや}に{通|かよ}っていた。
examples.english: When I was a child, my father would take me to the neighborhood barbershop.

notes:
Combines {散髪|さんぱつ} (haircut) + {屋|や} (shop, store). A casual word for a barbershop, especially the traditional kind for men. The suffix {屋|や} names a shop by what it sells or does.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {散髪屋|さんぱつや}に{行|い}く: to go to the barbershop
- {散髪屋|さんぱつや}で{髪|かみ}を{切|き}る: to get a haircut at the barbershop

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {理髪店|りはつてん}: barbershop — the more formal, signboard term
- {床屋|とこや}: barbershop — another common colloquial word, much like {散髪屋|さんぱつや}
- {美容院|びよういん}: beauty salon — offers cutting and styling for all genders
